why: Once you pick two drones, every even-indexed package must weigh exactly the first capacity and every odd-indexed one exactly the second. So count values separately on even and odd positions and keep the most frequent value in each group, with the two values forced to differ.
hints: Split the array into the even-index packages and the odd-index packages; each group is served by one drone.

Inside a group, the packages you keep are the ones already equal to the drone's capacity, so pick the group's most frequent value. The only catch: both drones must be different, so the two chosen values cannot be equal.
Count each group with a hash map and keep its top two (value, count) pairs. If the two leaders differ, keep both; otherwise try leader+runner-up both ways. Answer = n - kept. O(n) time.
pitfalls: All packages equal, e.g. [1,1,1,1]: the drones must be different, so one whole group gets replaced (answer 2).
A group with only one distinct value has no runner-up; treat its count as 0.
n = 1: the odd group is empty, answer 0.
statement:
Amazon has drones of every capacity from 1 to 10^9; drone j has capacity j. You must deliver n packages in order, where package i weighs pack[i].

You pick two different drones, and they alternate: the first takes packages 0, 2, 4, … and the second takes packages 1, 3, 5, …. A drone can deliver a package only if the package's weight is exactly its capacity (this is what the examples require).

You may replace any package with a package of any other weight. Choosing the two drones freely, return the minimum number of replacements so that every package can be delivered.

Worked example: pack = [3, 1, 3, 2].

  • Even positions hold [3, 3]; the best capacity for the first drone is 3 (both already match).
  • Odd positions hold [1, 2]; pick capacity 1 for the second drone (1 match), different from 3.
  • Only the package of weight 2 must be replaced (by weight 1): [3, 1, 3, 1]. Answer: 1.

For pack = [1, 1, 1, 1] the drones cannot both have capacity 1, so one group of two packages is replaced: answer 2.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • 1 ≤ pack[i] ≤ 10^9
  • The two drones must have different capacities.
